Name: Contact the Inquisition
Answer text: You report Father Lennart’s plan to the Inquisition.
Changes: Unrest -1, Spy Network -1, Reputation +1, Theology +1, Church -1

Title: Explosion
Text: A deafening rumble. The tinkling of broken glass. The pavement shudders beneath your feet. / Another explosion. | Sophia! What has she done?! | You struggle to understand what is going on. People stare in horror at the white cloud rising slowly above downtown Anizotte. / Magistrate El Verman’s mansion! / You run toward it. | The impact of the explosion is visible from several districts away. Houses and fences are crooked, and a grotesque mosaic of shattered glass litters the street. / Shrieks of terror. Moans of pain. | The air is still. A massive cloud of dust and gunpowder smoke blankets the entire noble district. / People stumble out of the haze covered in gray dust. They look like shadows. / Everything seems colorless — only the blood oozing from the victims’ wounds is of a vivid, scarlet hue. | A crowd of onlookers has already gathered around the ruins of El Verman’s mansion. / You notice Alida among them. She can hardly suppress a smile. | “This is the most powerful blow against the tyranny of the Empire I’ve ever seen!” | Where the Magistrate’s mansion once stood, there is now only a gaping hole full of rubble. Ripped from the ground by the blast, the pavement around the house resembles cracked eggshells. The neighboring homes have lost their exterior walls, the their rooms are exposed. | Gendarmes pull the bodies of those who have met their true death out of the wreckage, wrap them in coarse fabric, and load them onto wagons. / You feel sick. | You have never seen so many dead bodies before. / Mutilated in the explosion, they look only vaguely human. / You force yourself not to avert your gaze. | How many of them deserved this? How many just happened to be in the wrong place at the wrong time? / Servants, coachmen, simple passers-by… most of them must have been quite old… but still! / Did they really have to fall victim to Sophia’s plot? | Sophia chose the perfect target. / The murder of El Verman, an extremely powerful nobleman of ancient lineage, will not only remind the simple folk that the Last Straw is fighting tyranny; it will also instill fear in the defenders of the Empire. | Did you make the wrong choice? Should you have refused Sophia and prevented this disaster? / It is too late to change anything now.
Opens when: Unrest ≥ 8 and Sophia Has the Gunpowder and Sophia: not BETRAYED
On opening: Unrest +2, Power +1, Remy El Verman: TRUE DEATH

Title: The Greater Good
Text: It is nighttime. The print shop is empty. You sit by a lit candle, awaiting Sophia’s arrival. / She finally returns… | The door creeks. You can barely discern the smoldering embers of her pipe in the darkness. Her languid footsteps approach. / The glow of the candlelight falls across Sophia’s face. | “Hey there, [name].” | You take a step forward. The familiar smell of tobacco tickles your nostrils. / Sophia glances at the misericorde, her farewell gift. | “Still got it on you, huh? That’s good. You’ll need it soon enough.” | You raise your eyebrows inquiringly. | “It’s time I told you everything. Sorry I couldn’t confide in you until the last minute… I see I was wrong now.” | What in the world is she talking about? | “That moron Felipe had no idea there was a real revolt brewing right under his nose. Well, everything’s finally ready. We are ready, [name]! | “The Last Straw is tough now. Real tough. We’ve got firearms, manpower, an idea, and, most importantly, the people’s rage. There’s no stoppin’ it now! We just need to point it in the right direction, and… bam!” | You ask Sophia where she intends to direct this rage. | She stares at you. You cannot tell whether she is surprised or dismayed. | “Whaddaya mean, where?! At the Empire, of course! We’re gonna declare war! We’re gonna fight until there’s nothing left of the old order! / “We’re gonna fight until all those nobles are wiped out! Until the world finally changes! | “The half-measures guys like Egmont want ain’t gonna make the world better. / We’re doing this for the greater good! | “We’re gonna take the first step tomorrow. Felipe thinks he’s achieved his goals. He’ll order us to start his fake revolt. / “But we’re gonna start our own revolt. A real one. / “We’ll take Felipe out, and then we’ll finally be free.” | Sophia takes your hand. She clenches it so hard, it hurts. | “I want you by my side, [name]. It’s payback time.” | Her eyes are fixed on yours. The golden reflection of the candle flame flickers in them.
Opens when: Unrest ≥ 9 and Sophia: GROWN CLOSE and Felipe El Ferro: not SAW YOUR LOYALTY

Name: Agree
Answer text: You will be with her until the end.

Name: Try to talk her out of it.
Answer text: The path Sophia wants to walk is a dead end. She has to stop.

Title: Mutually Beneficial Collaboration
Text: It is amazing the heights of power a man can ascend to without a title when he has all the resources of the Empire working for him. / The more loyally you serve Felipe, the more authority he delegates to you. | The spy network covering the entire city has achieved astonishing results. / You appear to be an all-seeing prophet. Nothing and no one can escape your keen eye. / It is intoxicating. | Thanks to you, Felipe’s power grows with every arrest, every conviction, every execution. / The Secret Chancellery proves to the citizens and the Overseer time and again that Anizotte is swarming of insurgents. / And it is the only organization that can protect the Empire from the renegades.
Opens when: Spy Network ≥ 8 and Felipe El Ferro: SAW YOUR LOYALTY

Title: Clean Hands
Text: You have been pacing your office for an hour, lost in thought. The pieces of the puzzle finally fit. / Sophia managed to conceal her plans until the last moment, but after the incident with the firearms, everything came to light. | Sophia made her decision after leaving the city. She assembled a unit of people who were loyal to her personally, chosen from among the Magran insurgency. Mayer Egmont helped her transport the firearms from Eliria to Anizotte. / The spies you sent to verify this confirmed your deductions. Posing as refugees, Sophia’s people are flocking to the city. | It is evident that as soon as Felipe gives the word to proceed with the revolt, Sophia will transform it from a counterfeit rebellion into a genuine uprising. / If this happens, the streets of Anizotte will run red with blood. The firearms will grant Sophia’s insurgents a decisive advantage even against Arknian soldiers. | You get up from your chair and gather your papers. Felipe is expecting you to deliver your report in person. / You must not keep the advisor waiting.
Opens when: Unrest ≥ 3 and Spy Network ≥ 8 and Felipe El Ferro: SAW YOUR LOYALTY and Power ≤ 0 and one of: Sophia: GROWN CLOSE or Sophia: TRUE DEATH

Name: Keep Sophia’s secret
Answer text: You conceal what you have learned from Felipe.
Changes: Spy Network -3, Unrest +2, Willpower -5, Felipe El Ferro: BETRAYED

Name: Kill Sophia
Answer text: You reveal Sophia’s plan to Felipe and dispose of the out-of-control rebel together.

Title: Glory to the Empire!
Text: Sophia is dead. There is no one else capable of thwarting Felipe’s plans. | After several days of agonizing suspense, you finally receive a short note. | “It’s time.” | Day one. Preparations. | Messengers, letters, couriers… you need to get them all together. | Strangers come to you and give you passwords. / They ask for instructions, but usually they ask for money they can use to bribe, negotiate, and pressure. | Pamphlets. Slogans. Lists. Plans. Notes. Maps. Somber faces. Men. Women. Elderly people. Adolescents. / What an enormous number of people you’ve recruited over the years! | You have to remember to relate everything to Felipe. You can barely stay awake… | Day two. Instructions. | The rebellion needs to be spectacular. / Plenty of running around, shouting, and breaking windows. / Bloody brawls. / A few flashy fires. The key is not to overdo it. / The whole affair should take three or four hours, not more. | The riot has to be easy to put down. / What you need is a crowd. Ringleaders like Alida and Fuad should march in the front, accompanied by small groups. / They will wear headbands so they can easily be identified by Felipe’s men. | Those two actually believe that, as the leaders of the revolt, they are supposed to wear the red headbands so the other conspirators can effortlessly spot them in the crowd… / How stupid can you get? | When inspiring other people to rebel, you sometimes get carried away and find yourself believing in your own words about liberty and freedom from the Lots. / But, during your rare moments of solitude, you have to suppress the inappropriate pricks of conscience brought on by your own hypocrisy. / It’s okay. It's not that hard. | Day three. The revolt. | Felipe accused Mayer Egmont of treason against the Empire. The penalty is true death. / The dead body of the man who presided over the Lesser Quorum and did so much to help the people of Magra now dangles in front of the Chancellery. | The time has come. / The news of Egmont’s death is the spark that starts the fire. | The Last Straw begins to march. | Smoke is rising over the city. The crowd is raiding noble houses and temples of the Old Faith. / The Last Straw is getting ready to assault the Chancellery. A special squad is about to attack the city arsenal. / Everything is going according to plan. | You are amazed to see how smoothly this performance is playing out. / Horrified by the angry mob, the nobles hide in their luxurious mansions. / The clergymen of the Old Faith lock the doors of their temples to keep the heretics out. / The loyal lowborn subjects of the Emperor flee, fearing their own neighbors. | They need not worry, however. / The curtain is about to fall. | The square in front of the Chancellery. / The rebels are celebrating their victory. In a moment, the banner of the Revolt will fly! | But the cries of joy are drowned out by clattering hooves and clanking armor. | The noble militia, Anizotte’s finest warriors, enter the square. | The people panic. They push and shove. / There are futile efforts at resistance. | The steel fist of the nobility nips the revolt in the bud. | The Armory, the source of the weapons the insurgents so desperately need, turns out to be empty. / The battalions of the city garrison cut off the Last Straw’s escape route. | The rampaging crowds that once looked so threatening now scatter under the very first blows from the gendarmes. / There is no one to lead the rebels, no one to encourage them to resist. / The determination of these people accustomed to a life of obedience vanishes in the blink of an eye. | By the time the sun sets, silence reigns in the city. / But this is not the end. | Day four. El Ferro strikes. | The Last Straw is sent to the dungeons. Expert torturers from the capital extract all the necessary confessions from them. / Felipe makes his move. | The advisor lances all the Empire’s boils one by one. | The Lesser Quorum goes down first. / Their connection to the Last Straw is enough for the upstart merchants to be hanged as traitors. / With the Lesser Quorum gone, there will be no more need to humor the lowborn — ever. | The New Faith, the cancer that has spread throughout this city, is next. Not even the Silver Tree could cleanse its venom from Magra. / But Felipe can. / Lennart will be hanged for fomenting rebellion — Magra does not need another Fotis. / Any clergyman who dares to object will follow his pastor to the gallows. | The last strike Felipe delivers is directed at his long-time enemy Augustin El Borne, a criminal who has betrayed his noble Lot. / His laws have put the Empire in jeopardy, and he no longer has the faith of the people or the Overseer. / Now demoted to a simple judge by Gaius Tempest and stripped of the nobility of the Sword, he can harm the Empire no more. | The enemies of the Empire have been captured and defamed. / It is time for the trial. | The last day. Execution. | A fresh breeze in your face — there is nothing more precious under the merciless Magran sun. / The view from the rooftop of a house near the Chancellery is magnificent. From this spot, the teeming crowd looks like a river flooding the streets. | The square is not big enough to accommodate everyone who has come to watch. / The citizens of Anizotte are here to see the execution of the insurgents. | All the instigators of the revolt are lined up on a long scaffold. / Nooses swing heavily in the wind before them. | Abbot Lennart, whose pristine white cassock has been replaced by a filthy prison garb. / Fragile Alida and frail Fuad, who still cannot believe this is really happening. / Many, many people who devoted their lives to this pointless rebellion. | Felipe’s voice rouses you from your contemplation. | “Is the Overseer waiting for the entire province to show up? It’s time to finish this. The heat is unbearable.” | An old Arknian — Gaius Tempest, the Emperor’s Overseer in Magra — walks up to the stairs of the Chancellery and faces the crowd. / The people fall silent. / Even Baron El Ferro lowers his voice to a whisper. | “Guess he’s finally satisfied with the size of the audience…” | Gaius Tempest addresses the crowd in a rich baritone. The people devour his every word. | “I am the protector of my subjects, and I always will be. / “I have never been a butcher or a tyrant. In keeping with the teachings of the Twins and Isatius, it is my Lot to be a ruler and a warrior. / “And, as a warrior, I must fight our enemies. | “The people who were convicted today chose to rebel against me. / “They chose to rebel against the Emperor. / “They chose to rebel against everything the Empire stands for. | “But the Empire has loyal defenders who can discern the darkest of plots. They captured these insurgents and heretics and thwarted their murderous, meaningless riot. / “Today, I thank them for their service.” | The Overseers pauses. | “Nobility is one thing, but he’s not above using fear. Magra is in good hands now, [name].” | You nod. | “The punishment for these traitors against the Empire is true death by hanging. May the sentence be carried out before the gaze of the Younger!” | The executioner pulls the lever. The trap door swings open. / The prisoners plummet through the floor and dangle, suspended in midair by the nooses. / You hear their necks snap. | The insurgents are on their way to the Foot of the Pillar. | The crowd applauds obediently. | Everything is as it should be. | “That was a fine execution. What a relief, eh, Brante? | “By the way, I have something for you.” | The advisor reaches into an inner pocket and pulls out two documents. / He immediately gives you one of them. | “This is an official pardon for the crimes you committed in Eterna. / “You are now a free man. Use your new life wisely.” | You glance at the other document. / And what is this? / Felipe grins. | “This is an order giving you a job at the Secret Chancellery, [name]. | “You see, I’m getting older. I need a successor. / “Someone loyal, but smart. Someone who isn’t afraid of blood and difficult decisions. Someone who knows how to achieve his goals. Someone who understands the great burden we bear. / “You shook my hand once, and it paid off. What do you say now?” | Felipe offers you his hand. | You shake it without a moment’s hesitation. | “I’m pleased to welcome you to the service, [name] Brante. / “With defenders like you, the Empire will stand for all eternity.”
Opens when: Unrest ≥ 3 and Spy Network ≥ 8 and Felipe El Ferro: SAW YOUR LOYALTY and Power ≤ 0 and Clean Hands: Kill Sophia and one of: Sophia: GROWN CLOSE or Sophia: TRUE DEATH
On opening: Order +5, Power -3, Church -2, Wealth of Magra +3, Mayer Egmont: TRUE DEATH, Father Lennart: EXECUTED

Title: A Dangerous Haul
Text: Now that Archduke Milanidas has yielded in his struggle for power, the city of Anizotte is enjoying a moment of respite. / But your gut tells you to stay on your guard. / The powerful Arknian noble has relinquished some of his power, and someone will surely make an attempt to seize it. | You tell your people to watch the city closely and report anything even slightly suspicious to you right away. / At first, they mistake your unease for unfounded paranoia. / But your gut feeling soon proves to be true. Late one night, Alida barges into the print shop, clearly excited. | “Fuad’s found something big. You’ve got to see this!” | She takes you to the North Gate. / Fuad is waiting for you in a dark backstreet next to a sizeable wooden crate. / The old man lifts the heavy lid with a groan. | “Here, my friend. Take a look…” | You take a step closer… and freeze involuntarily. / Alida manages a nervous chuckle. / Fuad wipes beads of sweat from his brow. | Inside the crate are at least two dozen gunpowder muskets, along with bullet pouches full of lead balls. / With a couple of kegs of gunpowder, this would be enough to arm a full squad. | You cannot help but recall the convicts’ revolt in Eliria three years ago. / Nowadays anyone even suspected of owning a firearm similar to the guns they used is sent to the gallows at once. | Where did Fuad find all this?  / The old man lifts a finger, eager to enlighten you. | “So I was doing my watch, just like you asked, in a nice little place by the gate. / “And then I see a loaded wagon with three sturdy fellows on it. They look every bit like your ordinary workmen — except there’s something funny about ’em. | “They keep whispering and fidgeting, all odd-like. So I think: maybe they’re the Last Straw, right? I wanted to shush them, tell them to calm down, but the Twins told me I better wait. / “And them — bam! They get stopped by a patrol! | “The gendarmes keep asking them questions. Before you know it, they ask to see what’s in the crate. Well, that was that! | “The youngsters were all over the gendarmes before I could blink, and they did a real number on them, I tell you what! / “The gendarmes barely managed to cry for help before they all got knocked out. | “Then the guys started bickering. They ended up dumping the crate down an alley and scattering. / “The gendarmes came to and stumbled after them. Everybody forgot about the crate. / “I thought I ought to see what all the fuss was about. When I saw what was in there, I dragged the crate off to the side and called for you right away.” | You give the packing crate a closer look and notice a trademark branded on the side. / This is a crate from one of Mayer Egmont’s mines. They usually contain silver. | So Egmont is smuggling firearms into the city now, and men who know about it are being hunted by the Prefecture. They will not be able to hide for long. / And once they are finally caught, it will not be long before Felipe hears about these weapons. | You stare at the guns, lost in thought. / Where did Egmont procure these weapons? Are there more of them stashed throughout the city? / You might not have all the answers, but you still have to do something.

Name: Report this to Felipe
Answer text: You give him the crate of guns and track down the men who smuggled it into the city.
Changes: Unrest -1, Spy Network +1, Power -1, Felipe El Ferro +1, Mayer Egmont: ARRESTED

Name: Inform El Verman about this

Title: Usual Suspects
Text: Felipe has chosen an unusual meeting place tonight. / Anizotte’s ancient marble bathhouse is a place only nobles are allowed to enter. But tonight, in accordance with the advisor’s will, its doors are open to you. | The staff treat you with the subservience typically reserved for real noblemen. / You are shown to a magnificent hall with a ceiling supported by centuries-old columns and left alone. | The reflections of hundreds of candle flames dance across the walls and the water in the marble pool. You notice a bowl of candied fruit and a bottle of wine. / There are no other patrons. | This is most likely the only time you will ever see the inside of the bathhouse — Felipe rarely uses the same meeting place twice. / After a while, you muster enough courage to enter the water. | It is very warm. / You lie on your back and float. Your body relaxes, and a pleasant feeling of drowsiness creeps over you… | You are startled by echoing footsteps and the percussive thudding of a cane. / Felipe is approaching. Several burly men lead by Oliver Moss follow behind him. | You get out of the water and reach for your clothes, but Moss steps onto your garments, preventing you from covering yourself. | “Hello there, Brante.” | Felipe’s men surround you. | The advisor taps the floor with his cane. The sound echoes off the marble walls. / Droplets of water from your wet hair run down your back, causing you to shiver. | “Are you really naive enough to think you could conceal your betrayal from me, Brante? | “I’m the advisor of the Secret Chancellery. I know all about the deals you made behind my back. / “But I’ll give you one last chance to save yourself. Confess your betrayal, and maybe, just maybe, I won’t drown you in this pool like a runt.”
Opens when: Felipe El Ferro: not SAW YOUR LOYALTY

Title: A Sleepless Night
Text: Even late at night, the streets of Anizotte echo with chatter. The city cannot sleep. / You cannot sleep tonight either. | Advisor El Ferro sent you a surprising note a few hours ago: he is coming. | You hear slow, steady footsteps accompanied by the tapping of a cane. There is a knock at the door. Felipe enters the print shop. / Sophia quietly follows him in. You exchange a nod. | The print shop is crowded despite the late hour. / Father Fuad, Alida, and the other workers observe Felipe uneasily. Oliver is there too. He acknowledges the baron with a polite nod. / You suddenly realize that Felipe no longer cares at all if the Last Straw members see his face. | You walk into your office with Felipe and Sophia and lock the door. | “Well then, Brante. I hope your people are ready. It’s time to put our plan into action.” | “They’re ready. Just give us the word.” | “Excellent. Excellent. Soon our song of victory will reach its final note! | “Our road has been a long once, much longer than we thought, but now the end is in sight. / “I had a word with the Overseer, and in the end I managed to convince him that El Borne simply cannot maintain order in Anizotte. | “We are just one step away from being granted special authority for the Secret Chancellery. All we need is an excuse for action. / “Prepare your people, and take to the streets! | “And when I finally get that authority, we will eliminate each and every traitor to the Empire. Egmont, Lennart, El Borne — all of them! | “But those scum will probably try to flee Anizotte… I’ll need the people you’ve recruited throughout Magra, Sophia.” | “There are more than enough of them.” | “I’m glad to hear that. / “How much time do you need to prepare, Brante?” | You shift your gaze from Felipe to Sophia. She has been standing behind him all this time, a silent shadow with her head held high, her eyes trained on you. / Felipe’s cane taps the floor impatiently. He is waiting for an answer. | The advisor is right… the day you have worked for all these years has finally come. / Are you ready? What will you do now?

Name: Murder Felipe
Answer text: This is your chance to break free of the Secret Chancellery and spark a real revolt in Anizotte.

Title: The Last Straw’s Revolt
Text: Freedom — so intoxicating, so easily sliding into lawlessness. The desire for freedom infiltrates minds and hearts like a poison, leading people to commit monstrous crimes. / Freedom is like fire — in untrained hands, it can burn everything down. | The Chancellery now bears the banner of the Last Straw: a hand clutching a lantern, its beam cleaving the darkness. | The body of Felipe El Ferro is chained to the Chancellery gate for all to see. There is a wooden wheel on his stiff neck — the mark of the Secret Chancellery. / The mob is eager to pelt the advisor’s corpse with stones. | The gendarmes seized Mayer Egmont in first few hours of the revolt. / He was swiftly sentenced to true death for treason against the Empire and beheaded. | His head was put on a stake in front of the Lesser Quorum to frighten the people into submission. / But it did not work. The common people have seen Mayer Egmont as their protector for years now. His death has only enraged them. | The people fill the streets. Tempers run high, thanks in no small part to the Last Straw’s provocateurs. / A spark has fallen on dry tinder… and now the entire city has caught fire. | With Felipe dead, the authorities are helpless against your uprising — just as planned. / The Legion, the noble militia, the Prefecture gendarmes… they can do nothing to stop the revolt. / Your guns and gunpowder have crushed their every attempt to restore order. | Sophia’s little army has defeated the Empire’s first attempt to resist your movement. / And now, for one brief moment, the Last Straw holds sway over the entire city. | Together with Sophia, you step out onto the Chancellery’s tall stairs in the evening sun. / The square is crowded, teeming, full of people, all of them shouting ecstatically. / The time has come to pass judgment. | Sophia raises an arm. Her eyes are glowing, brighter than ever before. / The crowd falls silent. | “Listen, everybody! / “The nobles will never dare to oppress the commoners again! We’ve got weapons. We’ve got men. / ”We are the Last Straw. The old world order is about to come to an end! | “Today they tried to stop us on our way to freedom. They will be punished by the People’s Court!” | One by one, your people drag Felipe’s thugs out before the crowd and make them kneel in the dust. You spot Moss among them, glancing around like a cornered beast. / The mob screams in their faces. | “The people you see before you are loyal lapdogs of the Secret Chancellery. They all served the man who now hangs on the fence behind me. / “Today, we will put them on trial.” | Your men line up before the prisoners. / You give the command: ready! | “Please, [name]! Spare me! I wanna live! I was always faithful to you. I don’t deserve to die!” | “Enemies of freedom! For crimes against the people of Anizotte, we the People’s Court hereby sentence you to true death!” | You raise an arm: aim! / The gunmen train their muskets on the prisoners. | “What say you, judges?” | The people in the crowd pump their fists in the air. The cacophony of disparate voices merges into one. / “Death!” | “The People’s Court has spoken.” | You drop your hand. | The guns fire all at once. | Bodies fall to the ground. | The mob watches in awe as blood begins to drip down the Chancellery stairs. The bodies remain, forever dead. / And then they scream in terror and glee — a choir of voices so deafening, it makes the nearby windows shake. | The word of the people has become the Law. | “We cannot be stopped. We have tolerated the tyranny of the Empire for far too long! The time has come to take our destiny into our own hands. Those imperial bastards can’t stop our righteous revolution! / “Arm yourself, people! Your freedom is in your hands!” | You walk down the stairs, accompanied by the cries of the people. | “Friedemund, take the men and tell everyone to leave the square, then get to the city walls. We need to get all the gates under control. Gaius Tempest is probably already on his way here with his battalions.” | “Aye-aye!” | Sophia turns to you. Although utterly exhausted, she still manages a smile. | “I told you I was nothing but trouble… even I don’t know what’s gonna happen next.” | It doesn’t matter anymore, you tell her. Now you will either win or hang. No two ways about it. / Sophia laughs. | “Well said… / “I got an urgent job for you, [name]. We’ve done well, but our foothold here is still too weak. If our enemies decide to work together, we’ll be crushed. / “We need to split up. | “I’ll arm the new recruits. Friedemund will defend the walls. / “You keep an eye on the city. We have to finish off our enemies here in Anizotte and find new allies to support us.” | You promise to do everything you can. | Sophia’s fingers lightly brush against your cheek. Title: A Free Man

Title: The Revolt Begins
Text: Dawn in breaking. Title: The Family’s Fate
Text: The first rays of the morning sun reach the windows of your family home. It would be so easy to forget about the impending Revolt here within these old, familiar walls... / But the calm before the storm will soon be over, and yesterday’s turmoil will return. / There are only a handful of hours left. The Brantes have to decide what to do. Should the family stay in the city and prepare to weather the storm? Should they join the struggle? Or should they simply avoid it? | After a sleepless night, you gather in the sitting room as a family once again. / Father is the first to speak. His determined, yet surprisingly calm voice fills the room. | “This is what I was afraid would happen. The noble estate has turned a blind eye to the common people’s misery... and now we have a Revolt on our hands. / “It is my fault as well. I did all I could to serve the cause of justice... but it just wasn’t enough. And now blood will be shed.” | The family patriarch casts a somber gaze over his children. | “I want to make one thing very clear: today, our family cannot get involved in the unrest. We will not take sides. | “I feel for the common estate, but we’re not getting dragged into a hopeless bloodbath. / “As for preserving the Overseer’s rule in Anizotte... we will not sacrifice ourselves for that either. He has led Magra to this rebellion, and now it’s up to him and his Legion to deal with the rebels. | “And we mustn’t forget Commander Otton and his noble militia — they’re all too eager to use this opportunity to slaughter all the nobles they blame for the Revolt.” | Father is silent for a while. Then he takes his sword off the wall and places it firmly on the table. / His voice rings with the coldness of steel. | “We will stay in our city and protect our home. / ”Whatever danger we might face today, the Brantes will not surrender their home, their status, or their place in this world!” | None of you have ever seen Father so filled with resolve. But he still seeks your support. / Robert, the patriarch of the Brante family, meets your gaze. | “My son... I know you’re going to make your own decision. You’re too deeply involved in this conflict to just stand aside. / “But right now, I’m talking about our family here, [name]. Our family must remain out of harm’s way, no matter what you decide to do!”

But even in my darkest hour, I knew They hadn’t turned away from our world. / “I knew They still cared...” | Nathan is quiet for a moment, watching a tiny ant make its way across the porch. | “But I just can’t understand, no matter how hard I try... what’s happening to us? Please help me understand!” | Nathan’s sullen gaze rises toward the Shining Pillar, but thick, gray storm clouds are already moving toward the city. The shining strip at the edge of the sky is growing dimmer by the second. / You watch the sky too, lost in thought. / What will you tell him?

Title: Escape from Anizotte
Text: The house where you were born and raised is empty now. / All the supplies, clothes, and valuables you need for the journey have been packed into an inconspicuous-looking carriage. / The horses neigh nervously at every sound, every shout echoing down the street. | Father puts a heavy lock on the gate of the house. / He takes one last look at the estate, with its covered windows and boarded-up doors, then turns to you. | “We’re ready, son. I’m afraid it won’t be easy to get out of Anizotte.” | Your carriage hurtles down the perilous streets. / Places and faces flash outside the small windows. You see bands of armed commoners... preachers with crowds gathered around them... nobles on horseback, scrambling to defend their homes... | “I never thought I’d have to abandon our home... to leave our city behind, lost in chaos and confusion... / “What happened to our world, [name]? They are armed not with knives and clubs, but muskets. / One of them shouts an order as soon as he spots the carriage. The guards train their weapons on you. | “Hey you! So you can hightail it to the Legion and the Overseer and beg for help? / “I don’t think so! Now beat it, and pray to the Twins we don’t get you!” | With a dozen muskets trained on the carriage, you have no choice but to stop. | “What were we thinking? Answer text: You assemble a band of fighters from the Last Straw — people who are loyal to you and you alone. You'll lead them to fight for the Revolt.
Requires: Scheming ≥ 16 and Path of the Lotless and not The Defender of the Empire

Name: Support the Old Believer priests
Answer text: The priests of the Old Faith must struggle against the Revolt and stop the people from violating their sacred Lots.
Requires: Theology ≥ 16 and Path of the Priest and not Torch of the New Faith and not The Rebel

Name: Unite the nobles
Answer text: Right now, the noble bloodlines only care for their own safety. You have to unite them in the struggle against the Revolt.
Requires: Diplomacy ≥ 14 and Path of the Nobleman and Ennobled by the Sword and not The Rebel

Name: Buy the people’s loyalty
Answer text: With enough coin, you can convince at least some of the commoners to help you supress the Revolt.
Requires: Manipulation ≥ 14 and Wealth ≥ 3 and Path of the Lotless and not The Rebel

Name: Bide your time
Answer text: You decide to bide your time an avoid taking a side for now.

Title: To Arms
Text: The time has come. / A long and arduous day looms before you. You will need all the support you can get. / It is time to distribute your stash of guns and gunpowder to those you can truly trust. | You guide your loyal Last Straw comrades to the secret warehouse. / They dig into the contents enthusiastically, arming themselves with guns and hanging pouches of bullets from their belts. | You are now in command of an armed squad of loyal commoners. / Today they will help you reach your goal.

Title: A Fading Light
Text: The sun rises higher and higher. / Your carriage is hurtling down the street, making its way through the crowd with great difficulty. Many barricades have appeared overnight, made of old boards and rotten trash. / You have to reach the Prefecture as soon as you can. The gendarmes’ and judges’ reaction to the Revolt could be decided at any moment. / Any word from Sir El Borne — no, even the slightest sign from him — could determine their allegiance. | The Silver District is empty now, populated only by a searing wind sweeping light debris across the cobblestones. You smell smoke — a noble house must have been set on fire nearby. You hear hooves clattering in the distance. / There is not a soul around. / All you can hear is a fountain burbling in a small square... mixed with gentle, melodic laughter. | You yell for the carriage to stop. | Those graceful movements... that clothing, so light and airy... that thin, slender figure, playing and splashing in the water... / The rays of the sun dance and glitter on its golden skin. | That hot, carefree day flashes before your eyes... the sound of the carriage on the cobblestones... the handkerchief dropped on the ground... | Does Octavia still remember how you first met? / This creature... does it still have anything in common with the prideful Arknian lady you met here all those years ago? | The creature that was once Octavia is laughing, as though she cannot see the ruined streets around her. | You come closer. / You feel a strange, involuntary sense of calm next to this bizarre creature. There can be no hatred in her presence, no pain, no suffering. | She raises her large, pitch-black eyes to you. / Her voice rings with genuine elation. | “Do you see it all crumbling now? It’s the old world dying, collapsing under its own weight. / “Do not fear it. It’s not a bad thing. This is how it has to be. | “You live in the dream of the one called Octavia Milanidas, human who bears the name of Brante. This dream will end soon. And then it will all be gone — your Empire, your estates, your Lots, your Shining Pillar... | “And you, human named Brante, will be gone too. And the great mind of the La-Tari will leave this dream and move on, beyond all borders, beyond all limits. / “What great joy that moment will bring us!” | The creature that was once Octavia stretches her thin arms toward the horizon, where smoke already wafts against the backdrop of the sky. The screams of the rioting crowd are drawing closer. / This being is not of this world, and it is utterly helpless... especially here in Anizotte, in the middle of a rebellion. / The fate of the woman you knew as Octavia Milanidas is in your hands now.

Name: Hand her over to the Inquisition
Answer text: The soul of Octavia Milanidas has lost its way. Only the priests can help her now.
Requires: Octavia Milanidas: not SPIRITUAL BOND and not The Rebel

Name: Get her out of the city
Answer text: You must rescue the creature that was once Octavia from the flames of the Revolt. But the only one who can rescue the Archduke’s daughter from the city is Dorius Otton, the Archduke’s long-time ally…
Requires: Diplomacy ≥ 16 and Dorius Otton ≥ 0 and not The Rebel
Changes: Willpower -5, Nobles +1, Dorius Otton +2, Octavia Milanidas: BROUGHT BACK

Name: Share a final moment with her before she leaves this world
Answer text: If your beloved wants to leave this world, then so be it. You will accept her decision. But perhaps she can leave something behind, impart some kind of wisdom about her newfound existence before her departure.
Requires: Octavia Milanidas: SPIRITUAL BOND and one of: Theology ≥ 14 or The La-Tari Ritual

Name: Part ways with her
Answer text: The destiny of this transcendent creature is none of your concern now.

Title: Sir El Borne’s Choice
Text: It is noon. / A large crowd has gathered in the Prefecture square. / The gendarmes form a line in front of the stairs, clutching their cudgels nervously. | The commoners keep coming. The mob keeps growing. / They call out to the windows of the Prefecture. Their screams are deafening. / “El Borne sides with the people!” / “Gendarmes! Judges! Join us!” / “The people need you! It’s now or never!” | The rebelling citizens demand that the prefect take a side. / This decision must not be made without you. You have to get inside. / You push your way through the dense crowd until you reach the gendarmes. | “Oh! Sir Brante! I thought you’d been captured. / “Men! Let the judge through! | “Tell the judges to make up their minds! The people haven’t attacked us yet, but you never know...” | The main hall of the Prefecture is stuffy and crowded. The din of voices is as loud here as outside. / Almost every judge in the province is here now, save for those who stayed home or fled the city in advance. / Most of them demand that the prefect disperse the crowd. | Augustin El Borne is on the podium in the courtroom, looming above the indignant judges. | “No! I will not sic the gendarmes on the people! It is the Prefecture’s duty to listen to the Emperor’s subjects, not force them to be silent! / “If we disperse this crowd, it will only fan the flames!” | “And what of the Overseer’s orders, Sir Prefect? We have to quash the Revolt while we still can! / “Tell the gendarmes to do their duty and protect the city from these riots! | “Or do you want this so-called ‘People’s Court’ to hang us all? / ”Have you forgotten about the Last Straw and that freak Sophia? They’re executing people left and right, as though they’re wielding the divine Law! / “Do you really think you’ll be spared?” | The judges applaud Fockegraben — even those you believed to be the prefect’s most ardent supporters. | “This unrest needs to be quelled with words, not clubs! / “If we turn this demonstration into a bloodbath, there will be no stopping the carnage!” | El Borne tries to respond, but cries of outrage drown out his words. / The prefect frowns in consternation. The wrinkles on his forehead grow deeper. / He casts another glance around the courtroom and notices you standing in the doorway.

Name: Await El Borne’s decision
Answer text: You will not intervene. The Prefect can make this decision on his own.

Name: Convince El Borne to side with the rebellion
Answer text: You convince the Prefect to openly side with the Revolt.
Requires: Common Folk ≥ 1 and Valor ≥ 18 and Augustin El Borne ≥ 2 and not The Defender of the Empire
Changes: The Revolt +1, Troops +1, Common Folk +1, Nobles -1, Augustin El Borne: REBEL

Name: Support El Borne’s plan
Answer text: You speak out in support of the Prefect. He can calm the mob. The people will listen to him.
Requires: Augustin El Borne ≥ 2 and one of: Nobles ≥ 1 or Reputation ≥ 7

Name: Condemn El Borne
Answer text: It is the duty of every judge to follow the Overseer’s orders and suppress this revolt by any means necessary!
Requires: Diplomacy ≥ 18 and not The Rebel and not Branded by Dishonor
Changes: Common Folk +1, Augustin El Borne: DEFENDER OF THE EMPIRE

Title: A Cornered Beast
Text: Noon approaches. / Your thoughts keep returning to Sophia as you muster your forces for the impending fight for the city’s future. / Where is she right now? What are her plans? What are her orders for the Last Straw? | Joined by your followers, you carefully make your way through the now-empty streets. Danger could lurk behind any corner. | You take another turn and hear someone moaning in pain. You quickly zigzag to the edge of the Silver District. At the end of the street is a square in which several wooden stakes have been hastily erected. / Nailed to each stake is a commoner dressed in bloodied, tattered rags. | What is going on here?! / You sign for your men to take cover by the wall of an old factory. | You hear the hooves of a single horse clattering along the cobblestones. / A stately horseman rides toward the stakes, a luxurious cloak draped across his shoulders. You have know his dire form since you were a lad. / The Arknian’s arrogant voice echoes through the square. | “People of Anizotte! Heed my words! I am Dorius Otton, High Commander of Magra, leader of the noble militia!” | Otton points the tip of his sword at the writhing commoners. | “These lowborn wretches dared to sneak into the Silver District and rob noble homes! But I will not grant them the mercy of a lesser death by my blade. They will live and suffer as befits their Lot. This is their divine duty. | “Know this, rebels: anyone who follows your precious Sophia will share the same fate! / “I know my runaway servant’s wily ways. She’ll send you all at me without a second thought, and you will all die by my hand! She won’t care. She’s completely insane! All she wants is to see Anizotte burn to the ground!” | Your men exchange uneasy glances. / You motion for them to remain quiet. You need to stay out of sight for now. | “Sophia! I know you’re around here somewhere. You’ve grown up, but you’re still my property. I can see your people turning their backs on you. All hope is lost. / “Come back to your lord and master! You will be mine forever!” | The lone rider is motionless and silent in the empty square. / It is quiet. Even the captive commoners stifle their moans. | Bang! | A squad of Last Straw rebels spills out of an alleyway and rushes at Otton. / Sophia is the first among them, her plain shirt stained with blood, a long, heavy musket in her hands. | “You lying, blue-faced whoreson! I want him alive — the People’s Court will deal with him!” | Sophia stops and takes aim. / Another gunshot rumbles. / Otton’s mare collapses, wounded, taking her rider to the ground. | The rebels run toward Otton, celebrating his downfall. / But then you hear the deafening clacking of hooves coming from the Silver District. / The noble militia! The riders were waiting to ambush Sophia! | The elite cavalrymen smash into the Last Straw squad like a heavy steel gauntlet. / The rebels are taken by surprise. They are about to retreat. / Otton gets up from under his horse, his sword at the ready. | “Not one step back, damn you! We’ll fight them to the end!” | The militia has the rebels and their leader surrounded. / Your people are hugging the wall, trying to stay out of sight. They watch the fight anxiously, awaiting your orders. | It is time to act. / If Sophia is captured, she will not be there to lead the rebellion. However, if she escapes, the Revolt will be ruled by her merciless, vindictive cruelty. / This is about more than just Sophia, you remind yourself. This confrontation could decide the fate of the entire Revolt.

Name: Rush to Sophia’s side
Answer text: You come to Sophia’s aid and rescue her squad from the ambush.
Requires: Troops ≥ 1 and one of: Sophia: LOVER or Sophia: ALLY
Changes: The Revolt +2, Troops +1, Willpower +5, Sophia: LEADING THE REVOLT

Name: Get rid of Sophia
Answer text: Sophia is in your way. You will deceive her and hand her over to Otton.
Requires: Scheming = 20 and Troops ≥ 1 and one of: Sophia: LOVER or Sophia: ALLY
Changes: Troops +1, Common Folk -1, Dorius Otton +2, Sophia: CAPTIVE

Name: Stop Sophia
Answer text: Sophia’s wrath will be the death of your entire cause and herself as well. You rescue Sophia from the ambush, hoping you can talk some sense into her and take control of the rebellion.
Requires: Troops ≥ 1 and Manipulation = 20 and Sophia: LOVER
Changes: Troops +1, The Revolt -1, Willpower -5, Sophia: HOPEFUL

Name: Order a retreat
Answer text: You are staying out of this. Whether Sophia gets out of this or not is up to her.
Changes: The Revolt +1, Willpower +5, Sophia: LEADING THE REVOLT

Name: Capture Sophia and have her executed
Answer text: Sophia is cornered, trapped. You will snatch her from Otton’s clutches only to eliminate her yourself.
Requires: Troops ≥ 1 and Sophia: not LOVER and one of: Valor ≥ 14 or Scheming ≥ 20
Changes: The Revolt -4, Troops -1, Power -1, Willpower -5, Sophia: EXECUTED

Title: The Order, Divided
Text: It is noon. The wind drives the sand along the stone slabs. / The Inquisition has gathered inside the yard of the ward, but they are uneasy. The schism within the church has split the Order as well. / Some of the inquisitors follow the Old Faith, while others are New Believers. Their contentious quarreling can be heard over the ward’s tall fence. | “We need to stay in the ward and protect ourselves until the Overseer’s army comes!” / “But we cannot abandon the people at a time like this! It is our duty to stay with the faithful and preach on the streets!” / “We need to show our support to the noble militia! They’re the ones protecting the Order!” | “The rebels are fighting for the legitimacy of the New Faith! We’re done being persecuted!” / “It is the Will of the Twins that Lennart become Patriarch! We cannot stop him!” | The ward’s doors open. Jeanne briskly walks outside. | “Enough! | “It was I, brothers and sisters, who brought the Inquisition back to power in Anizotte, and you all know it! But now it pains me to see what we have become! | “I have never taught you to be cruel. I used to believe that each and every Inquisitor knew their sacred Lot, that you all saw the Wrath of the Gods looming ever so close, that you all knew what They could do to our world should we besmirch Their design! / “But, clearly, I was wrong. | “This city is full of heretics. The Inquisition has failed. The time for talk is over. There will be no more words, no more prayers... no more mercy. / “I am taking control of the Order, and and it will smite the heathens! | “Lennart will stop at nothing to become the new Patriarch — even if it means defiling our sacred ceremony. / “We will stand in the way of his procession. Not a single one of those rebels will reach the Silver Tree!” | “But, Inquisitor, Lennart will have crowds of people on his side. The Champions of Faith won’t be able to stop them!” | “Then the inquisitors will have to take up arms as well!” | The inquisitors meet her words with stunned silence. / Finally, someone speaks up hesitantly. / “But what about our Lot? We cannot wield weapons in battle! Do you realize what this means for our souls, Jeanne?” | “Our Lot? It is our Lot to guide those who have strayed and save their souls — even if it means our own souls must be damned to eternal torment at the Foot of the Pillar! | “The fate of our flock depends on what we do at this fateful hour. If we must defy our Lot and sacrifice ourselves to avert the Wrath of the Gods, then so be it!” | Jeanne points an accusing finger at the inquisitors who espouse the New Faith. | “Captain Agaronim — seize the heretics!” | The Champions of Faith do as they are told. / They force the wayward inquisitors to their knees. / The other priests watch in confusion. | “We shall begin by purging this heresy from our Order. / “Then we will head to the Silver Tree. Lennart and his flock must not enter the Temple, lest our world be doomed!” | You walk through the gate. / Jeanne’s furious eyes dart toward you.

Name: Convince her to spare the inquisitors
Answer text: You persuade Jeanne to spare the New Believers kneeling before her.
Requires: not The Defender of the Empire and not Cassius Faces the Tribunal and one of: Eloquence ≥ 20 or Jeanne: GROWN CLOSE
Changes: The Revolt +1, Church +1, Clergy +1, Common Folk +1, Willpower -5, Jeanne +1

Name: Free the captive inquisitors by force
Answer text: You order your followers to attack and save the captives.
Requires: Troops ≥ 1 and not The Defender of the Empire and one of: Torch of the New Faith or Cassius Overthrown
Changes: The Revolt +2, Troops -1, Church +1, Clergy +1, Common Folk +1, Jeanne -2

Name: Seize control of the Order
Answer text: You and Jeanne take control of the Inquisition. The heresy must be purged, even if it means violating your Lot.
Requires: not Cassius Overthrown and not The Rebel
Changes: The Revolt -1, Troops +1, Church -1, Clergy -1, Jeanne: DOOMED FOR HER SIN

Name: Stop Jeanne
Answer text: You convince Jeanne to change her mind before she violates her Lot.
Requires: Theology ≥ 18 and Cassius Faces the Tribunal and not The Rebel and one of: Jeanne ≥ 4 or Jeanne: GROWN CLOSE
Changes: Troops +1, Church -1, Clergy +1, Willpower -5, Jeanne: RIGHTEOUS

Name: Do not get involved
Answer text: You let Jeanne decide for herself.
Requires: not Cassius Overthrown and not The Rebel
Changes: The Revolt +1, Willpower +5, Jeanne: DOOMED FOR HER SIN

Name: Accept death
Answer text: You are one of those whom Jeanne seeks to destroy. You cannot escape this fate.

Title: The Prefecture under Siege
Text: The searing sun looms high in the sky above the rebellious city. | The square in front of the Prefecture is packed with commoners. / Just a moment ago, they boldly demanded that the judges and gendarmes side with the Rebellion. / But now they are terrified. They fear the noble army that is coming for them. Their calls for rebellion are gone, replaced by frightened screams. | Hooves thunder against the cobblestones. / The earth quakes beneath their feet. | The noble militia led by Dorius Otton carves a path through the human sea. / The terrified rebels scatter as the riders approach. | The gendarmes remain where they are, forming a tight circle around the Prefecture and El Borne. / The prefect calls out to the crowd, his voice hoarse. | “Everyone, stay calm! Let them through! Do not draw your weapons!” | Otton’s riders push the mob aside and eventually reach the tall building. / The Arknian commander draws in his reigns only when the gendarmes all that separate him from the Prefecture stairs. | “Prefect El Borne! How dare you disobey the orders of the province’s rightful rulers? You have abused your position to appease the rebels and defy Imperial rule. / “This inconceivable rebellion is your fault! | “It’s time for you to accept your well-earned punishment. / “In the name of Archduke Milanidas, I hereby order you and your gendarmes to surrender your weapons!” | The supreme judge of the Prefecture maintains his composure in the face of this recrimination. | “I only obey the laws of the Empire, Sir Otton — not you or your runaway Archduke!” | Otton’s face contorts into a predatory grin. | “Excellent. You’ve had your chance to save face, old man. / “Instead of a dignified execution, you and your cronies will hang — like the foul rabble you’ve betrayed us for!” | Otton lifts his sword skyward, prepared to order an assault. The riders behind him are about to attack. / The gendarmes ready their clubs. Their hands are trembling. They will not stand a chance against the noble cavalry. / The mob begins to shift, about to flee the square. / The fate of this moment hangs by a thread.

Name: Rouse the mob and encourage them to defend the prefect
Answer text: El Borne has always protected the common folk. Now it is time for them to protect him.
Requires: Common Folk ≥ 2 and Willpower ≥ 0 and Augustin El Borne: not DEFENDER OF THE EMPIRE and not The Defender of the Empire
Changes: The Revolt +2, Troops +1, Power +1, Order -1, Willpower -5, Augustin El Borne: REBEL

Name: Get Otton’s army to abandon him
Answer text: Otton has been stripped of his rank. You reason with the nobles and convince them to abandon their leader.
Requires: Otton is Sentenced and not The Defender of the Empire and one of: Nobles ≥ 1 or Diplomacy ≥ 16
Changes: The Revolt +1, Troops +1, Power +2, Nobles +1, Common Folk +1, Order +1, Dorius Otton: TRUE DEATH, Augustin El Borne: REBEL

Name: Challenge Otton to a duel
Answer text: It is time to settle your feud with Otton once and for all.
Requires: Nobles ≥ 1 and Augustin El Borne: not REBEL and Otton Faces the Court of Honor and not The Rebel

Name: Overthrow El Borne
Answer text: You help Otton bring the prefect down for good.
Requires: Troops ≥ 1 and Willpower ≥ 0 and not Otton Faces the Court of Honor and not The Rebel
Changes: The Revolt +1, Order -1, Nobles +1, Power -1, Dorius Otton +2, Augustin El Borne: TRUE DEATH

Name: Get Otton and El Borne to reconcile
Answer text: If Otton and El Borne both want to put an end to the Revolt, they should abandon their feud and join forces.
Requires: Diplomacy = 20 and Reputation ≥ 6 and Dorius Otton ≥ 0 and Augustin El Borne: not REBEL and not The Rebel and one of: Night of the Serpents or Broken Chains
Changes: The Revolt -1, Power -2, Order +1, Nobles +1, Common Folk -1, Willpower -5, Augustin El Borne: DEFENDER OF THE EMPIRE, Dorius Otton: RECONCILED

Name: Stay out of it
Answer text: You observe their conflict as an indifferent bystander.
Changes: Power -1, Order -1, Willpower +5, Augustin El Borne: TRUE DEATH

Title: The Duel with Otton
Text: The prefect’s voice booms over the square, raspy with tension. / The greatest enemy of the rite of single combat has no choice but to announce the duel. | “Dorius of the Otton dynasty and [name] of the Brante bloodline will now cross swords in mortal combat! I summon their ancestors to bear witness to their duel! / “May their Blood Tides meet in sacred battle and determine the truth. May the Younger witness our trial and behold the power of His inevitable Law!” | The mob that surrounds you falls silent. The whispering wind is the only sound you hear. / There is no more time for solemn ceremonial bows. You and your foe are about to clash in a merciless battle. | “You’ve got quite the nerve, Brante, crossing the lines like that. I know that full well. But how you will fare in a real fight...” | Before finishing his sentence, the Arknian lunges at you with a rising slash, swift as a venomous snake. | You vividly recall Otton’s trial by combat at castle Enerie — he tried the same trick on Gaius Tempest! / You lean to the left quickly, dodging the mortal blow. | Otton bares his teeth and strikes again, faster than lightning. / You manage to parry his lunge. Sharpened steel screeches against steel. / Yet the Arknian’s inhuman strength ultimately overwhelms you. He pushes until the edge of his blade bites into your shoulder. | Cold steel slices through your jacket and sinks into your flesh. / But you manage to fight through the pain. With a burst of strength, you shove Otton’s blade away. | The two of you stand face to face, panting loudly. Warm blood drips down onto your clothes. / There are whispers in the mob. “ Brante’s done for! Why did he even challenge an Arknian?” | Otton allows himself an arrogant chuckle. | “Your blood is weak, Brante. But what do you expect? Once a commoner, always a commoner. Your grandfather was born a peasant, and your father never became a true nobleman... | Slowly, Otton creeps toward you, preparing to strike again. / The Arknian’s cold eyes glint with adamant confidence in his own superiority. His sword flashes in the light of the sun, heralding your impending demise. / You assume a fighting stance again, mustering the last of your strength. / The next moment will decide the outcome of the duel.

Name: Defeat Otton
Answer text: Your skill with the sword is great — great enough to rival even the most skilled swordsman in Magra.
Changes: The Revolt -1, Troops +1, Power -1, Nobles +1, Common Folk +1, Willpower -5, Dorius Otton: KILLED IN A DUEL, Augustin El Borne: DEFENDER OF THE EMPIRE

Name: Call upon your forebear
Answer text: Otton’s bloodline gives him strength, but you are not alone in this battle either.
Requires: Valor ≥ 16 and Gregor Brante ≥ 2 and Ennobled by the Sword
Changes: The Revolt -1, Troops +1, Power -1, Nobles +1, Common Folk +1, Dorius Otton: KILLED IN A DUEL, Augustin El Borne: DEFENDER OF THE EMPIRE

Name: Die with honor
Answer text: You cannot win, but you will face your inevitable end with honor, for the sake of the Brante bloodline.

Name: Overcome death
Answer text: You muster all your inner strength to defeat the Arknian.
Changes: The Revolt -1, Willpower -20, Nobles +1, Troops +1, Common Folk +1, Power -1, Dorius Otton: KILLED IN A DUEL, Augustin El Borne: DEFENDER OF THE EMPIRE

Title: The March of the New Faith
Text: An enormous sea of humanity flows through Anizotte, filling the streets of the Temple District. / They are led by Abbot Lennart. | The New Believers walk peacefully behind him, many of them women and the elderly. They are unarmed. Their faces show neither fear nor anger. / They are so drastically unlike the throngs of rebels who are currently ransacking streets and looting noble houses. | The procession slowly makes its way toward the temple at the Silver Tree. / The Temple has always been where patriarchs of the Church accept their sacred duty, along with the heavy burden of responsibility for their flock before the Twin Gods. | When a Patriarch speaks, the Twins pay heed. / And every eight years, it falls upon the Patriarch to proclaim in Their sight how Their world is humbly following the Lot it has been given. | Long, long after the Twins descended to our world, the patriarchs came to be elected at the Conclave by the clergy. This tradition has continued for many years. / Today dozens of priests have come to the Temple in spite of the unrest to conduct the rite and spare the Twins’ world from Their wrath. / But now thousands of commoners are walking to the same temple to elect the new Patriarch themselves. | You and your followers take a side street to the temple, avoiding the immense procession. | Soon the square by the Tree is packed, teeming, overwhelmed. / But the stairs to the Temple doors cannot be reached — a stalwart phalanx of Champions of Faith blocks the way, with Jeanne in the lead. / They are joined by the inquisitors — those who have decided to walk the path of the Old Faith until the very end. | “I will not allow you into the Temple, Lennart. / “These heretics will not make you patriarch!” | Father Lennart slowly begins to ascend the stairs. / He does not argue with Jeanne. The abbot simply faces her with a humble smile and gestures at the people standing behind him. | Doubt clouds the Champions’ faces. / Lennart’s procession is truly staggering. Even if they are mere commoners, even if they are unarmed and empty-handed, there are simply too many of them to be stopped by a few dozen Old Believers. | “Sister Jeanne... look at them. / “Are they truly heretics? All of them? They are just people, our brothers and sisters in Faith! / “Why would the Inquisition treat us like enemies? We do not reject the Twin Gods — nay, we seek Them with our every thought.” | “You rejected the Law of the Younger when you chose to seek your own Lots!” | “No, Jeanne! The only thing we reject is Isatius’s error!” | “This argument has been going on for years, Lennart. I know each and every point you can make. Don’t even bother. / “You will not enter the Temple. | “And all these people... you’re just dragging them down to the Foot of the Pillar along with you. How can you still not understand this after so many years? What do you think you’re doing, Lennart?! / “Don’t you fear the Wrath of the Gods?” | “I do not, Jeanne. When I become Patriarch, I will tell the Twins that we still love and revere Them just as we always have, even as we seek a different path to Them. / “The Twins will hear us. They will listen. They will understand. / “There will be no Wrath of the Gods!” | The New Believers heed Lennart’s words. They begin to firmly ascend the stairs to the door of the temple. / The Champions’ swords do not deter them. | Jeanne watches the massive congregation approach her, her eyes filled with remorse. / She raises an arm, about to give her final order. | “Champions of Faith! Protect the sacred Temple! Fight to the bitter end!” | You reach the foot of the stairs as she speaks these words. / This is your last chance to intervene.

Name: Lead the procession to the Temple
Answer text: Lennart will become Patriarch. The clergy will support his candidacy.
Requires: Clergy ≥ 2 and Common Folk ≥ 2 and Eloquence ≥ 16 and not The Defender of the Empire and one of: Cassius Overthrown or Torch of the New Faith
Changes: Troops +1, Common Folk +1, Nobles +1, Church +1, Father Lennart: PATRIARCH, Jeanne: DEFEATED

Name: Stand with Jeanne and drive the procession away
Answer text: Allowing the common folk to elect the patriarch is an affront to the Twin Gods. The Inquisition and the clergy will never let that happen!
Requires: Troops ≥ 1 and Clergy ≥ 2 and Jeanne: RIGHTEOUS and not The Rebel
Changes: The Revolt -2, Troops +1, Church -1, Nobles +1, Common Folk +1, Power -1, Father Lennart: DEFEATED

Name: Save the New Believers from bloodshed
Answer text: You need to try to get these people away from the Temple!

Title: The Rebel Leader
Text: The sun is setting. / The blood-red sky quavers in the hot smoke from the fires raging throughout the city. / You cannot help but recall a passage from the Lives of the Twins, one of the many pages Mother used to quote when you were a child. / “And the Elder said, ‘Lo, I have cast a flame into the world, and I shall guard it until it begins to blaze.’” | Could this passage be referring to today? | You lead your followers to Empire Square. / You walk around rubble, past abandoned carriages and unfinished barricades. / There have clearly been clashes here recently — the dust of the departed is still rising into the sky. | Thousands fill the square before the Chancellery — well over half the commoners of Anizotte. / The Chancellery has been under rebel control since noon. All Imperial officials either fled or were torn apart by the mob. | Scraps of rumors and gossip reach your ears as you move closer. / “Did you hear what happened at the great Tree?” / “It’s the inquisitors! They just started slaughterin’ folks! They grabbed them swords o’ theirs and started killin’ unarmed people!” / “Lennart’s procession made it into the Temple! There was a sign from the Twins!” / “All lies! The Twins got angry and destroyed ’em all under the Tree! The temple’s gone, I tells ya, gone for good!” | The crowd is on edge. Any dispute could explode into a brawl. / A voice from the Chancellery stairs calls for another People’s Court. The mob turns as one. | Several Last Straw rebels drag a handful of well-dressed nobles out onto the steps and force them to their knees. / The leader of the executioners is a preacher with a mane of unkempt hair and the wild eyes of a lunatic. | “The Younger! The Younger, he speaks through us, He does! He gave us the power of His Law — the power to punish our enemies, to execute them! / “Anyone who stands in our way is an enemy of the Twins Themselves! | “People! It’s time to judge these enemies of the simple folk. What is your sentence?” | The mob roars so loudly, the square shakes. / “Death! True death!” | The Last Straw rebels ready their guns. / One of the captive gets to his feet and speaks out defiantly. | “You dare call this pathetic freak show a People’s Court? You don’t have the power — you never have, and you never will! You think you can wield the Law of the Twins? Bah! We’ll come back, and we’ll make you pay...” | The aged nobleman’s last words are drowned out by a thunderous volley of gunfire. / One by one, the nobles collapse, their bodies pierced by bullets. They remain where they fall. / The mob gasps in amazement. / There can be no doubt — the People’s Court has the power to mete out true death at will! | “This is what will happen to anyone who dares to oppose us! All hail the Revolt! All hail our leader! All hail Sophia! | “Sophia’s gonna lead us. She’s gonna fend off the Legion! She’s gonna bring justice — first to Anizotte, then to the whole Empire! She’s gonna tear down the old ways and wipe all them tyrants and nobles from the face of the world!” | The mob explodes into an ecstatic chant. / They shout one word over and over again: | “Sophia! Sophia!” | The enormous throng bellows wildly, eager to see the face of its leader.

Title: Hearth and Home
Text: While you are busy preparing, night falls over Anizotte. / The darkness brings disorder, lawlessness, and chaos. | In the dark, madmen, robbers, and looters flood the city. These gangs have no interest in the fate of the Empire or the Revolt. / They see the uprising as a sign that the end of the world is nigh. / And if the Wrath of the Gods is at hand, then everything is permitted. | Upon hearing reports of gangs roaming the streets, you sense danger. / What is to stop them from attacking your home? / Your people may need you, but you will never abandon your family! | Taking a squad of loyal men with you, you hurry to your home district. / Your instinct proves to be correct. Even before reaching your street, you smell smoke. | Sir Tibor’s school is ablaze. The old man was hurled out a third-story window and impaled on the sharp spikes of the gate below. / Ashes from dozens of burning books blanket the ground like black snow. | Tommas’s old house lies in ruins. / Breathless, you run up the street. Your men can barely keep up with you. / You hope you are not too late... | You round the last turn. / There it is, the gate of your ancestral home! | You see dozens of figures approaching by the light of the burning houses. / The thugs are close — too close! | You run through the gate and into the house. | Your men stay to guard the outside. / You hastily open the door. | Your father is on the doorstep, sword in hand. / He recognizes you and lets out a sigh of relief. | “It’s you, [name]! I’m so glad you’re here! The bastards have burned down half the district, and they’re on their way here...” | He is cut short. / The living room window is shattered. A torch lands on the floor. / You quickly stamp out the flames. | A battle is in full swing in the front yard. / A massive crowd is furiously attacking your soldiers without any regard for their own safety. | The looters are led by a rugged, half-naked old man clad in rags. Horrible scars on his wrists and ankles reveal his past as a convict. / He yells franticly in your direction, his shrieks cutting through the din of the fray. | “The world is coming to an end! We’ve disobeyed the Twins, and they’re punishing us. There ain’t no punishment worse than this, so there ain’t nothing to fear! These are our last hours! Do whatever you want!” | The crowd bellows in support of the old man. / Your soldiers fall one after another beneath the onslaught of the rabid gang. | “The Twins have damned us all. We’ve been damned for your sins, you filthy nobles, you false priests! / “But before we face our final judgment, we’ll dole out a little punishment of our own, hee hee hee! We’ll take our revenge on you before we die. Title: The Battle for Anizotte
Text: The dark void beyond the walls of Anizotte is lit by hundreds of lights. / Heavy boots tread the soil. Armor clanks. Halberds gleam. Drums beat a lively march. / Lit by the glow of the torches, the Magran Legion approaches the city walls. | Gaius Tempest himself leads the Legion. It is the Overseer’s duty to crush the Revolt this very night and pacify the city before news of the incident spreads throughout the Empire. / If the Overseer’s hesitation allows the Revolt to last even a few days, it could jeopardize not only his position, but even the fate of the entire province that has been entrusted to him. | An entire city rebelling against Imperial rule... nothing like this has happened for generations. | The people of Anizotte tremble in fear before the punishment that will befall them if the Legion wins. / You have done your utmost to crush the revolt on the streets. / The crowds in the squares have been dispersed. The riots and fires have stopped. The armed commoners clamoring for freedom as the sun set have now scattered and locked themselves in their homes. | But the main forces of the Revolt have not been defeated yet. / There are still many insurgents who are ready to fight to the true death for their cause... | The soldiers of the Last Straw, reckless conspirators and dangerous fighters taught by Sophia to struggle against the old order until the bitter end. / Zealous New Believers who would rather face execution than betray their faith. / Poor nobles and former Legion soldiers who have joined the Revolt in violation of their oath of loyalty to the Empire. They know there will be no mercy for them, so they have nothing to lose. | The remaining rebel forces have gathered at a fortified base by the city gate. / The rebels have surrounded it with barricades, preparing to repel an attack from either side. / The soldiers of the Revolt, some armed with spears and axes, some with firearms, and some with simple rocks, hastily assemble atop the walls. / The rest of the city no longer supports them. But the revolt has not been crushed yet. | The Legion gets into formation in front of the gate, ready to begin the assault as soon as their commander gives the order. / The defenders atop the walls respond by raising their firearms. / A herald from Gaius Tempest comes forward, stopping mere steps from the gate. Title: The Battle for Anizotte
Text: The dark void beyond the walls of Anizotte is lit by hundreds of lights. / Heavy boots tread the soil. Armor clanks. Halberds gleam. Drums beat a lively march. / Lit by the glow of the torches, the Magran Legion approaches the city walls. | The Imperial army finally arrives to put an end to this unfathomable revolt.Gaius Tempest himself leads the Legion. It is the Overseer’s duty to crush the Revolt this very night and pacify the city before news of the incident spreads throughout the Empire. / If the Overseer’s hesitation allows the Revolt to last even a few days, it could jeopardize not only his position, but even the fate of the entire province that has been entrusted to him. | An entire city rebelling against Imperial rule... nothing like this has happened for generations. | The decisions you made today have compelled most of the people of Anizotte to join the Revolt. / By nightfall, the rebels have gained the upper hand. The defenders of the Empire have no hope of victory. / They may have amassed a considerable army to fight the Revolt, but they came too late. The troops loyal to the Empire have reached an impasse. The entire city has risen against them. | Exhausted and demoralized by the futile fight, many Imperial loyalists leave their camp or surrender to the rebels. | Only the inexorably approaching Legion separates the Revolt from total victory. / The time for rioting and lawlessness has passed — now all the forces of the Revolt have joined forces in pursuit of a single goal: / To hold the city! | The main forces of the Revolt maintain order in their camp with a firm hand. / There are still many insurgents who are ready to fight to the true death for their cause. | The soldiers of the Last Straw, reckless conspirators and dangerous fighters taught by Sophia to struggle against the old order until the bitter end. / Zealous New Believers who would rather face execution than betray their faith. / Poor nobles and former Legion soldiers who have joined the Revolt in violation of their oath of loyalty to the Empire. They know there will be no mercy for them, so they have nothing to lose. | All the remaining rebel forces gather at a fortified base by the city gate. / The rebels have surrounded it with barricades, preparing to repel an attack from either side. / The soldiers of the Revolt, some armed with spears and axes, some with firearms, and some with simple rocks, hastily assemble atop the walls. | The Legion gets into formation in front of the gate, ready to begin the assault as soon as their commander gives the order. / The defenders atop the walls respond by raising their firearms. / A herald from Gaius Tempest comes forward, stopping mere steps from the gate. He loudly proclaims the Overseer’s demands. | “My subjects! Lay down your arms this instant and open the gate! I know that you have been deceived by the insurgency. / “You have my word as an Arknian ruler that I will spare anyone who aids the Legion and turns over the leaders of the revolt. | “Should you disobey this order from your lawful ruler, none of you will escape disgrace, execution, and eternal torment at the Foot of the Shining Pillar!” | The Legion herald proudly lifts his head, awaiting the rebels’ decision. | You cast a quick glance at your allies. / The time for preparations has ended. Everything depends on the size of your army and the balance in the city between the forces you have managed to win over and those you have antagonized. / The next hour will determine your place in history.

Title: A New Day Dawns
Text: It is morning. / You stumble along a now-empty backstreet, utterly exhausted after the most trying night of your life. / An elderly stranger in a threadbare cloak shambles down the road in the opposite direction. | The old man looks around cautiously at every step, seemingly struggling to remember where he is going. / As you approach him, he suddenly stops and speaks to you. | “Good morning to you!” | You slow down for the old man and wearily return his greeting. | “May I ask you for a favor, my friend?” | You barely have any energy to waste today... but there is something about this old stranger’s voice that compels you to listen. / A favor? What kind of favor? | “Well, my brother and I had a disagreement, you see, and I want to know who was right. | “My brother says this world is already perfect as it is. The Twins made it like this, after all...” | The old stranger pauses, casting a glance over the street — the charred carcasses of buildings and homes, the overturned carriages, the dried bloodstains on the paving stones. | “And I told my brother that, no matter what Their initial design may have been, the world as it is now needs to change. | “So then my brother asked me, ‘what exactly needs changing?’ / “But I had no answer for him. | “So here I am, wandering around, tormented by this question. Would you help us settle our dispute, my good man? / “Who’s in the right here, me or my brother? | “If you were in the Twins’ place, what would you do? What about this world needs changing?”

Name: Say you would grant the world forgiveness
Answer text: Life is a long road, and mistakes are inevitable. The Twins ought to grant mortals hope for forgiveness.

Name: Say you would leave the world alone
Answer text: The Twins did create the world, but now They ought to leave Their creation in peace and refrain from meddling in the affairs of men.

Name: Say you would take better care of the world
Answer text: The Twins should never have been so distant from Their creation. Mortals need Their care, assistance, and supervision.

Name: Say you would free mortals from the Lots
Answer text: If it were up to you, you would make it known that everyone is free to choose their own Lot and their own path to the Twins.

Name: Say you would destroy the world
Answer text: The Twins’ creation is nothing more than a monstrous cage, a dark dungeon that dooms mortals to a life of suffering. If you had made this world, you would destroy it with your hands.

Name: Say nothing and walk away
Answer text: You leave the old man’s question unanswered.

I’ve got no more to lose. / The net is torn, the rusted bars are cracked. / I won’t forgive. For me, there’s no excuse. / You wanted this to end... now comes my final act.

Title: What Became of Gloria
Text: Gloria’s new life as a nobleman’s wife put an end to her youthful ardor. When she moved to her husband’s home, her fervent poetry and her struggle in the name of the common folk remained in the past. / She languished in her newfound monotony at first, mourning her fate. | But her connection to the Brante family remained. Through this surviving link, Gloria found the strength to overcome her alienation and pull herself out of the depths of melancholy in which she was mired. / Slowly but surely, she came to recognize and accept the genuine love of Sir Jose El Peletier, and in time she responded to his selfless and cordial care with deep gratitude. | Gloria eventually came to terms with her newfound life in the noble estate, far from the city. She soon gave birth to the first of their children and dedicated herself to raising the heir of the great El Peletier bloodline. / And so Gloria spent the rest of her life far from the turmoil in Anizotte, surrounded by comfort and warmth until the end of her days.

Title: What Became of Gloria
Text: After that unforgettable quarrel in the Brante home, Gloria left Anizotte to travel the Empire. / She hoped to see the life of the common folk firsthand and transcribe the truth in her travel notes. | The news of the Revolt back in Anizotte reached Gloria during her trip through the province of Eliria. She seized the opportunity right away and sparked an uprising against the crown among the local commoners. | However, the province’s noble militia swiftly suppressed the riots. / Gloria was captured and sentenced to hard labor in the mines for life. | But not even hard labor could stop Gloria. She did her best to inspire her fellow prisoners to rise up against their captors. / But, rather than share her fervor, the other laborers turned her in, hoping for a reduced sentence. | Gloria fought tooth and nail against the old ways, but she did not live long enough to see whether or not her efforts ever bore fruit. / Instead, she met a swift and ignoble end.
